Implement `partition_enrollment(csv_text)` in `solution.py` using only the standard library. The input is CSV text whose header must contain `given`, `family`, `contact`, and `tier`; otherwise raise `ValueError`. A non-string input raises `TypeError`. Empty text returns empty result lists without error.

Return a new dictionary with exactly `starter`, `experienced`, and `warnings`. Applicant entries are `(given, family, contact)` tuples. Preserve source-row order within each group. Trim surrounding whitespace in all four fields. Tier matching is case-insensitive: `starter` enters the first group, while both `experienced` and the accepted misspelling `experianced` enter the second.

A data row is malformed if it has missing or extra columns or any required field is empty. Skip malformed rows and append `row N: malformed` to `warnings`, where the header is row 1. Skip unknown tiers and append `row N: unknown tier <normalized-tier>`. Blank physical rows may be ignored without a warning. CSV parsing errors must be converted to `ValueError`. Do not print anything, mutate caller data, or reuse result containers across calls.

import unittest

from solution import partition_enrollment


class PartitionEnrollmentTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_empty_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(partition_enrollment(""), {
            "starter": [], "experienced": [], "warnings": []
        })

    def test_partition_trimming_spelling_and_order(self):
        text = (
            "given,family,contact,tier\n"
            " Ada , Lovelace , ada@example.test , STARTER \n"
            "Grace,Hopper,grace@example.test,experienced\n"
            "Katherine,Johnson,k@example.test,Experianced\n"
            "Alan,Turing,a@example.test,starter\n"
        )
        result = partition_enrollment(text)
        self.assertEqual(result, {
            "starter": [
                ("Ada", "Lovelace", "ada@example.test"),
                ("Alan", "Turing", "a@example.test"),
            ],
            "experienced": [
                ("Grace", "Hopper", "grace@example.test"),
                ("Katherine", "Johnson", "k@example.test"),
            ],
            "warnings": [],
        })

    def test_column_order_is_taken_from_header(self):
        text = "tier,contact,family,given,optional\nstarter,c@x.test,Fam,Given,x\n"
        self.assertEqual(partition_enrollment(text)["starter"],
                         [("Given", "Fam", "c@x.test")])

    def test_malformed_unknown_and_blank_rows(self):
        text = (
            "given,family,contact,tier\n"
            "A,B,a@x.test,mystery\n"
            "C,D,,starter\n"
            "\n"
            "E,F,e@x.test,starter,extra\n"
            "G,H\n"
            "I,J,i@x.test,  Other  \n"
        )
        result = partition_enrollment(text)
        self.assertEqual(result["starter"], [])
        self.assertEqual(result["experienced"], [])
        self.assertEqual(result["warnings"], [
            "row 2: unknown tier mystery",
            "row 3: malformed",
            "row 5: malformed",
            "row 6: malformed",
            "row 7: unknown tier other",
        ])

    def test_header_and_input_validation(self):
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            partition_enrollment(None)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            partition_enrollment("given,family,tier\nA,B,starter\n")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            partition_enrollment('given,family,contact,tier\n"unterminated,B,c@x,starter\n')

    def test_results_are_fresh(self):
        text = "given,family,contact,tier\nA,B,a@x.test,starter\n"
        first = partition_enrollment(text)
        first["starter"].append(("X", "Y", "z"))
        first["warnings"].append("changed")
        second = partition_enrollment(text)
        self.assertEqual(second, {
            "starter": [("A", "B", "a@x.test")],
            "experienced": [],
            "warnings": [],
        })
        self.assertIsNot(first, second)
        self.assertIsNot(first["starter"], second["starter"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
